⛳ BMW Championship Round 1 Is Live — Here's Everything You Need to Know

The second leg of the FedExCup Playoffs gets underway today at Bellerive Country Club in St. Louis. 50 players. 4 rounds. And the most important number in the field: 30.

Because the top 30 at the conclusion of Sunday's final round advance to the Tour Championship at East Lake in Atlanta, August 27-30. For everyone else, the season ends this week.

Here's where the standings stand entering Round 1:

No. 1 — Scottie Scheffler (4,873 FedExCup pts)
No. 2 — Matt Fitzpatrick
No. 3 — Cameron Young
No. 4 — Si Woo Kim
No. 5 — Wyndham Clark
No. 11 — Xander Schauffele
No. 13 — Rory McIlroy
No. 22 — Viktor Hovland

Scheffler is dominant. He won the St. Jude Championship in Memphis by eight shots and leads the field by nearly 1,400 FedExCup points. Short of a catastrophic collapse, he arrives at East Lake as the overwhelming favorite.

McIlroy is safe — his 13th place ranking means he has cushion — even after a disappointing 66th-place finish at St. Jude. McIlroy is a two-time defending Masters champion (2025 career Grand Slam + 2026 defense) and will be determined to finish the season strong.

The real drama is at the cutoff. Sepp Straka withdrew from the field for a family matter, which affects how the bubble calculates at positions 28-31. Any player currently ranked 28-35 is playing for their Tour Championship lives.

Bellerive CC plays as a par 70 at 7,448 yards — a demanding layout last used for this event in 2008. Get your scorecards ready. 🏌️

🇨🇦 CPKC Women's Open is LIVE — The Best Women's Field in the World is in Edmonton

Round 1 of the 52nd CPKC Women's Open tees off today at Royal Mayfair Golf Club in Edmonton, Alberta, and the field is as strong as we've seen at a women's major in years.

Here's who to watch:

🏆 Nelly Korda (World No. 1, +440 favorite)
The American enters with four wins in 2026 — including three majors: the Chevron Championship, Riviera May Open, and U.S. Women's Open. She's been the dominant force in women's golf this year and arrives at Royal Mayfair with everything going for her.

🍁 Brooke Henderson (Defending Champion)
Henderson won here in 2025 at Mississaugua, edging Minjee Lee by one shot with a closing 4-under 67 for her 14th career LPGA title. Now at 28 and playing in front of a home crowd in Edmonton, she's a legitimate threat to repeat.

🏅 Lydia Ko (Three-Time Champion)
Ko has won this event three times, including in 2013 as a 15-year-old amateur — the youngest LPGA winner in history at the time. She returns chasing a record fourth title.

The Canadian contingent this year is 15 players — the largest ever in the event's 52-year history. Organizers expect 75,000-80,000 spectators over the four days.

Six of the top 10 players in the world are in the field, including HyoJoo Kim, Miyu Yamashita, Ruoning Yin, Hannah Green, and Minjee Lee.

Par 70, 6,452 yards, $2.75M purse. Let's go. 🏌️‍♀️

🏌️ LIV Golf Indianapolis Is Underway at Pete Dye's Final Masterpiece

The 54-hole strokeplay event at The Club at Chatham Hills in Westfield, Indiana, gets underway today — and this is a course with a story. Chatham Hills was Pete Dye's final course design before his passing in 2020, a thoughtful and demanding layout that gives this LIV finale extra meaning.

Jon Rahm has already done the main thing: he clinched his third consecutive LIV Golf individual season championship before even arriving in Indianapolis. The Spaniard's dominance across the 2026 season has been total. This week is a victory lap.

But there's still a major storyline playing out. The 2026 LIV Team Championship is competitive:

🥇 4Aces GC (DJ/Pieters/Detry/A. Kim) — Season leader
🥈 Ripper GC (Smith/Leishman/Herbert/Smylie) — 2.25 pts behind
🥉 Legion XIII — Third

The team title will determine bragging rights, bonus money, and season legacy. For the players on these squads, Indianapolis matters.

Plus: Thomas Rhett performs on Friday, Disco Lines on Saturday. LIV Golf continues to blend sports and entertainment in a way that differentiates it from the traditional tour model.

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
LIV Golf's financial situation is dire.

Saudi PIF ending funding after 2026. Indianapolis prize money cut from $20M to $10.1M. Michigan Team Championship cancelled. Players reportedly waiting on payments.

The circuit's future is genuinely uncertain. #LIVGolf #Golf

facebook.long_form:
Posting window: 3:30 PM ET

💰 LIV Golf's Financial Future Is in Serious Jeopardy

New reporting confirms what the rumors had been suggesting: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund — which has invested approximately $5 billion in LIV Golf since the circuit launched — will end its financial backing after 2026.

The impact on this week's Indianapolis event is visible and stark:

📉 Prize money slashed: $20M → $10.1M (winner gets $2.02M instead of $4M)
❌ Michigan Team Championship: cancelled entirely
💸 ~$60M in promised prize money: gone
⚖️ Lawsuit: Fresh Tape Media filed suit July 21 in New York Supreme Court for $1.23M+ in unpaid fees for LIV Golf Week (January 12-14, West Palm Beach)
⚠️ Players reportedly awaiting payments

This is not a small development. LIV Golf was built on the promise of extraordinary prize money — it was the primary recruitment tool for attracting top PGA Tour talent. The financial model that made that possible is ending.

What comes next is unclear. LIV Golf has been in various stages of merger talks with the PGA Tour, and the financial pressure could accelerate or collapse those discussions. For the players who signed long-term LIV contracts based on financial promises, the uncertainty is real.

The circuit is still operational. The event is happening this week. But the era of unlimited Saudi backing appears to be ending — and nobody knows exactly what happens after 2026.

---

article.headline: LIV Golf's Financial Future in Jeopardy as Saudi PIF Ends Backing After 2026

Posting window: 6:00 PM ET

📊 FedExCup East Lake Bubble — Who's In, Who's Out, What's at Stake

One week from tomorrow, the Tour Championship begins at East Lake in Atlanta. The 30 players who survive the BMW Championship this week earn their spot. Everyone else goes home.

Here's the state of play heading into Round 1 today:

✅ SAFE (well inside the top 30):
• No. 1 Scottie Scheffler — dominant, 1,400+ pts ahead of No. 2
• No. 11 Xander Schauffele — comfortable cushion
• No. 13 Rory McIlroy — survived St. Jude despite a tough week (66th), still 13th overall

🔥 ON THE BUBBLE (positions 28-35 are contested):
• The math around the bubble was shaken by Sepp Straka's withdrawal (No. 5 FedExCup points). When a high-ranked player doesn't play, it means points from the event don't redistribute as expected.
• Players ranked 31-40 heading in need a strong finish to move inside the top 30 cutoff.
• A single top-10 finish this week can move a player inside or outside the bubble dramatically.

Bellerive CC plays as a par 70, 7,448 yards. Low scores are possible — the field is the best 50 players in golf this season. A -15 week might not even be enough if the leaders go deep.

One round is done by tonight. Check back for live updates. 🏌️

---
